label: def
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def}
	An  $R$-module $M$ {\rm{(}}not necessary $I$-torsion{\rm{)}} is called
	$ETH$-weakly cofinite with respect to an ideal $I$ of $R$ or $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite if
	$\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_{R}(R/I,M)$ is a weakly Laskerian $R$-module for all $i$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Let $I$ be an  ideal of $R$.
	\begin{itemize}\item[(i)]  All weakly Laskerian $R$-modules, $ETH$-cofinite and weakly cofinite $R$-modules with respect to ideal $I$  are $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite.
		\item[(ii)]  Suppose $M$ is an $I$-torsion  module,
		then $M$ is $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite if and only if it is $I$-weakly cofinite module.
	\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
{\rm{(}}i{\rm{)}}	Let $(R, \mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d>0$. Let
	$M=R\oplus E( R/\mathfrak{m})$. It is easy to see that $M$ is an $\mathfrak{m}$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite
	$R$-module  that is not  $\mathfrak{m}$-cofinite.
	
{\rm{(}}ii{\rm{)}} Let $(R, \mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d>0$. Let
$M=R\oplus(\underset{i\in \Bbb N}\oplus  R/\mathfrak{m})$. It is easy to see that $M$ is an $\mathfrak{m}$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite
$R$-module  that is not  $\mathfrak{m}$-weakly cofinite.

label: haj
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{haj}
	An  $R$-module $M$ is said to be weakly Artinian if its injective envelope, can be written as $\operatorname{E}_R(M)=\oplus_{i=1}^{k}\mu^0({\mathfrak{m}}_i,M)\operatorname{E}_R(R/{\mathfrak{m}}_i)$ where ${\mathfrak{m}}_1,\dots,{\mathfrak{m}}_k$ are maximal ideals of $R$.
head: environment

label: haj1
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: See \cite[Lemma 2.3 (b)]{Haj}.
head: environment

label: max
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
{\rm(i)}$\Longrightarrow${\rm(ii)}  follows by definition.
	
In order to prove {\rm(ii)}$\Longrightarrow${\rm(i)} note that

\begin{center}
	$ \operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))\cong \operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M).$
\end{center}

  Since $\operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))\subseteq \operatorname{Max}(R)$, it is easy to see that $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))$ is a weakly Artinian $R$-module and so by  \cite[Lemma 2.8]{Haj} $\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M)$ is also a weakly Artinian $R$-module. On the other hand by \cite[Theorem 6.1.2]{BSh} $\operatorname{H}^{i}_{I}(M)=0$ for all $i\geq 1$. Since any weakly Artinian  $R$-module is weakly Laskerian, therefore
  $\operatorname{H}^{i}_{I}(M)$ is $I$-weakly cofinite for all $i\geq 0$. Now by  \cite[Corollary 3.10]{Mel},
  it follows that $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(R/I,M)$ are weakly Laskerian for all $i\geq 0$, as required.

label: FD0
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By definition there is a finitely generated submodule $N$ of $M$ such that  ${\rm
		dim}(M/N)\leq 0$. Also, the exact sequence
	$$0\rightarrow N \rightarrow M \rightarrow M/N \rightarrow 0,\,\,\,\,\,\,(*)$$
	induces the following exact sequence
	$$0\longrightarrow {\rm Hom}_R(R/I,N)\longrightarrow{\rm
		Hom}_R(R/I,M)\longrightarrow {\rm Hom}_R(R/I,M/N)$$$$\longrightarrow {\rm
		Ext}^1_R(R/I,N).$$ Whence, it follows
		that the $R$-modules $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M/N)$ is weakly Laskerian. Therefore, in view of Lemma \ref{max}, the $R$-module $M/N$ is
	$I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite. Now it follows from the exact sequence $(*)$ and Lemma \ref{third} that $M$ is
	$I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite.

label: asli
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
{\rm(iii)}$\Longrightarrow${\rm(ii)} Using the exact sequence
$$0\rightarrow\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M)\rightarrow M\rightarrow M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M) \rightarrow 0,$$
we get the exact sequence
\begin{center}
$0\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))\longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,M).$
\end{center}
Since $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))=0$, it follows that the $R$-modules
\begin{center}
$\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M))$
\end{center}
are weakly Laskerian, and so in view of  \cite[Proposition 3.2]{BNS2} the
$R$-module $\operatorname{\Gamma}_I(M)$ is $I$-weakly cofinite. Now as the $R$-module $
\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,M)$ is weakly Laskerian, it follows from \cite[Theorem 4.1 (c)]{AM}
that the $R$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{1}_{I}(M))$ is weakly Laskeran. If $\mathfrak{p} \in \operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{1}_{I}(M))\subseteq \operatorname{Supp}_R(M)$, then 
$$\operatorname{H}^{1}_{IR_{\mathfrak{p}}}(M_\mathfrak{p})\cong\operatorname{H}^{1}_{I}(M)_\mathfrak{p}\neq 0.$$

Since $\dim M \leq 1$, it is easy to see that $\dim R/\mathfrak{p}=0$ or $\dim R/\mathfrak{p}=1$.  If $\dim R/\mathfrak{p}=1$ then $ M_\mathfrak{p}$ is a zero dimensional $R_\mathfrak{p}$-module that implies $\operatorname{H}^{1}_{IR_{\mathfrak{p}}}(M_\mathfrak{p})=0$  by using Grothendieck vanishing theorem \cite[Theorem 6.1.2]{BSh} which is a contradiction. Thus $\dim R/\mathfrak{p}=0$ and so $\mathfrak{p}$ is a maximal ideal. So we have the following inclusion 
$$\operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{1}_{I}(M)))\subseteq \operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{1}_{I}(M))\subseteq \operatorname{Max} R.$$
By Lemma \ref{haj1} (v), it is easy to see that the $R$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{1}_{I}(M))$ is weakly Artinian and
so by \cite[Lemma 2.8]{Haj} the $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^{1}_{I}(M)$ is weakly Artinian. Since any weakly Artinian module is weakly Laskerian, therefore in view of  \cite[Theorem 6.1.2]{BSh}  the $R$-module
$\operatorname{H}^{i}_{I}(M)$ is $I$-weakly cofinite for all $i\geq 0$.

{\rm(i)}$\Longrightarrow${\rm(ii)}  by  \cite[Corollary 3.10]{Mel},
it follows that $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(R/I,M)$ are weakly Artinian for all $i\geq 0$, as required.

{\rm(i)}$\Longrightarrow${\rm(iii)} It is obviously true.
head: environment

label: wl
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label {wl}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $M$ be an ${\rm
FD_{\leq 1}}$  $R$-module. Then $M$ is $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite if and only if
 $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M)$ and  $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,M)$ are weakly Lakerian.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By definition there is a finitely generated submodule $N$ of $M$ such that  ${\rm
dim}(M/N)\leq 1$. Also, the exact sequence
$$0\rightarrow N \rightarrow M \rightarrow M/N \rightarrow 0,\,\,\,\,\,\,(*)$$
induces the following exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow {\rm Hom}_R(R/I,N)\longrightarrow{\rm
Hom}_R(R/I,M)\longrightarrow {\rm Hom}_R(R/I,M/N)$$$$\longrightarrow {\rm
Ext}^1_R(R/I,N)\longrightarrow{\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,M)\longrightarrow {\rm
Ext}^1_R(R/I,M/N)\longrightarrow {\rm Ext}^2_R(R/I,N).$$ Whence, it follows that
the $R$-modules $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M/N)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(R/I,M/N)$ are weakly Laskerian. Therefore, in view of Proposition \ref{asli}, the $R$-module $M/N$ is
 $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite. Now it follows from the exact sequence $(*)$  and Lemma \ref{third} that $M$ is
 $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{2.2}
	Let $I$ be an ideal of a Noetherian ring $R$, $M$ a non-zero $R$-module and
	$t\in\Bbb{N}_0$. Suppose that the $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ is $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite
	for all $i=0,...,t-1$, and the $R$-modules ${\rm Ext}^{t}_R(R/I,M)$ and ${\rm
		Ext}^{t+1}_R(R/I,M)$ are weakly Laskerian. Then the $R$-modules ${\rm
		Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M))$ and ${\rm Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M))$ are weakly Laskerian.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use induction on $t$. The exact sequence 
	
	$$0\longrightarrow \operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M)\longrightarrow M \longrightarrow M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M)
	\longrightarrow 0,\,\,\,\,\,\,(*)$$
	
	induces the following exact sequence:
	
	$$0\longrightarrow {\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))\longrightarrow{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/I,M)\longrightarrow {\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/I,M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))$$$$\longrightarrow {\operatorname{Ext}}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))\longrightarrow{\operatorname{Ext}}^1_R(R/I,M).$$
	
	Since ${\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/I,M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))=0$ so ${\rm
		Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))$ and ${\rm Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))$ are weakly Laskerian. Assume inductively that $t>0$ and that we have established the result for non-negative integers smaller than $t$. By applying the functor ${\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/I,-)$  to the exact sequence $(*)$, we can deduce that ${\operatorname{Ext}}_R^j(R/I,M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))$
	is weakly Laskerian for $j=t,t+1$. On the other hand, $\operatorname{H}_I^0(M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))=0$ and $\operatorname{H}_\Phi^j(M/\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M))\cong \operatorname{H}_\Phi^j(M)$ for all $j>0$. Therefore we may assume that $\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(M)=0$. Let $E$ be an injective hull of $M$ and put $N=E/M$. Then ${\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R/I,E)=0=\operatorname{\Gamma}_\Phi(E)$. Hence  ${\operatorname{Ext}}_R^j(R/I,N)\cong {\operatorname{Ext}}_R^{j+1}(R/I,M)$ and $\operatorname{H}_\Phi^j(N)\cong \operatorname{H}_\Phi^{j+1}(M)$ for all $j\geq 0$. Now, the induction hypothesis yields that ${\rm
		Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}_\Phi^{t-1}(N))$ and ${\rm Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}_\Phi^{t-1}(N))$ are weakly Laskerian and so ${\rm
		Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}_\Phi^{t}(M))$ and ${\rm Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}_\Phi^{t}(M))$ are weakly Laskerian, as required.
head: environment

label: homext
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{homext} Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I\in \Phi$ an ideal of $R$. Let $t\in\Bbb{N}_0$ be an integer and $M$ an $R$-module such that $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/I,M)$ are weakly Laskerian for all $i\leq t+1$. Let the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ are ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$ $R$-modules for all $i<t$. Then, the following conditions hold:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)]  The $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ are $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite {\rm{(}}in particular $\Phi$-weakly cofinite{\rm{)}} for all $i<t$.
		\item[(ii)]  For all ${\rm FD_{\leq 0}}$ {\rm{(}}or minimax{\rm{)}} submodule $N$ of
		$\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)$, the $R$-modules $${\rm Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N)\,\,\,
		{\rm and}\,\,\,{\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N)$$ are weakly Laskerian. In
		particular the sets $$\operatorname{Ass}_R({\rm Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N))\,\,\, {\rm
			and}\,\,\,\operatorname{Ass}_R({\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N))$$ are  finite sets.
	\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) We proceed by induction on $ t$. In the case $ t = 0$ there is nothing to prove. So, let $ t >0 $ and the
result has been proved for smaller values of $t$. By the inductive assumption,
$\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ is $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite for $ i = 0, 1, ..., t-2$. Hence by Lemma
\ref{2.2} and assumption, ${\rm Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t-1}_\Phi(M))\,\,\, {\rm
	and}\,\,\,{\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t-1}_\Phi(M))$ are weakly Laskerian. Therefore by
Theorem
\ref{wl}, $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ is $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite {\rm{(}}in particular, $\Phi$-weakly cofinite{\rm{)}} for all $ i < t$. This completes the inductive step.\\
                                       
               
(ii) In view of   (i) and Lemma \ref{2.2},  ${\rm Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M))\,\,\, {\rm
	and}\,\,\,{\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M))$ are weakly Laskerian. On the other
hand, according to Lemma \ref{FD0}, $N$ is $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite. Now, the exact
sequence

$$0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow \operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N
\longrightarrow 0$$

induces the following exact sequence,
$${\rm
	Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M))\longrightarrow {\rm
	Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N)\longrightarrow {\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,N)\longrightarrow$$
$$ {\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M))\longrightarrow {\rm
	Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N)\longrightarrow {\rm Ext}^2_R(R/I,N).$$

Consequently  $${\rm Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N)\,\,\, {\rm and}\,\,\,{\rm
	Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{H}^{t}_\Phi(M)/N)$$ are weakly Laskerian, as required.\qed
head: manual

label: homext1
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{homext1} Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I$ an ideal of $R$. Let $t\in\Bbb{N}_0$ be an integer and $M$ an $R$-module such that $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/I,M)$ are weakly Laskerian for all $i\leq t+1$. Let the $R$-modules $H^i_I(M)$ are ${\rm FD_{\leq1}}$ ~ $R$-modules for all $i<t$.
	Then, the following conditions hold:
	
	{\rm(i)} The $R$-modules $H^i_I(M)$ are $I$-weakly cofinite for all
	$i<t$.
	
	{\rm(ii)} For all ${\rm FD_{\leq 0}}$ {\rm{(}}or minimax{\rm{)}} submodule $N$ of
	$H^{t}_I(M)$, the $R$-modules $${\rm Hom}_R(R/I,H^{t}_I(M)/N)\,\,\, {\rm
		and}\,\,\,{\rm Ext}^1_R(R/I,H^{t}_I(M)/N)$$ are weakly Laskerian. In particular the
	set $\operatorname{Ass}_R(H^{t}_I(M)/N)$ is  finite.

label: cof
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cof} Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I\in \Phi$ an ideal of $R$. Let $M$
	be an $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite $R$-module  such that the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$
	are ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$ $R$-modules for all
	$i$. Then,
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)] the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ are $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite {\rm{(}}in particular, $\Phi$-weakly cofinite{\rm{)}} for all $i$.
		\item[(ii)]  for any $i\geq 0$ and for any ${\rm FD_{\leq 0}}$ {\rm{(}}or minimax{\rm{)}} submodule $N$ of
		$\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$, the $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)/N$ is   $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite
		{\rm{(}}in particular, $\Phi$-weakly cofinite{\rm{)}}.
	\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i)  Clear.\\ (ii)  In view of  (i) the $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ is
$I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite for all $i$. Hence the $R$-module ${\rm Hom}_R(R/I,N)$ is
weakly Laskerian, and so it follows from Lemma \ref{FD0} that $N$ is
$I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite. Now, the exact sequence

$$0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow \operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)\longrightarrow \operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)/N
\longrightarrow 0,$$

and Lemma \ref{third} implies that the $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)/N$ is $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite.\qed
head: manual

label: cof1
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cof1} Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I$ an ideal of $R$. Let $M$
	be an $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite $R$-module  such that $R$-modules $H^i_I(M)$ are ${\rm
		FD_{\leq1}}$  $R$-modules for all $i$. Then,
	
	{\rm(i)} The $R$-modules $H^i_I(M)$ are $I$-weakly cofinite for all $i$.
	
	{\rm(ii)} For any $i\geq 0$ and for any ${\rm FD_{\leq 0}}$ {\rm{(}}or minimax{\rm{)}} submodule $N$ of
	$H^{i}_I(M)$, the $R$-module $H^{i}_I(M)/N$ is  $I$-weakly cofinite.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I$ an ideal of $R$. Let $M$ be
	an $R$-module such that  the $R$-modules $H^i_I(M)$ are ${\rm
		FD_{\leq1}}$ $R$-modules for all $i$. Then, the following conditions are equivalent:
	
	{\rm(i)} The $R$-module $M$
	is an $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite.
	
	{\rm(ii)} The $R$-modules $H^i_I(M)$ are $I$-weakly cofinite for all $i$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) Follows by  Corollary \ref{cof1}.

(ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) It follows by \cite[Proposition 3.9]{Mel}.\qed
head: manual

label: cof2
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cof2} Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I\in \Phi$ an ideal of $R$. Let
	$M$ be an $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite $R$-module  such that  $\dim M/IM \leq 1$ {\rm(}e.g.,
	$\dim R/I \leq 1${\rm)} for all $I \in\Phi$. Then,
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)] the $R$-modules $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ are $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite {\rm{(}}in particular, $\Phi$-weakly cofinite{\rm{)}} for all $i$.
		\item[(ii)]  for any $i\geq 0$ and for any ${\rm FD_{\leq 0}}$ {\rm{(}}or minimax{\rm{)}} submodule $N$ of
		$\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$, the $R$-module $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)/N$ is   $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite
		{\rm{(}}in particular, $\Phi$-weakly cofinite{\rm{)}}.
	\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) Since  by \cite[Lemma 2.1]{BZ1}, $$\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)\cong\underset { I \in \Phi}
	\varinjlim \operatorname{H}^{i}_I(M),$$ it is easy to see that $\operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M))
	\subseteq\underset{I \in \Phi}\bigcup \operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{i}_I(M))$ and therefore
	$$\operatorname{dimSupp} \operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M) \leq \sup \{ \operatorname{dimSupp} \operatorname{H}^{i}_{I}(M)| I \in
	\Phi \} \leq 1,$$ thus $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ is ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$ $R$-module
	and the assertion follows by  Corollary \ref{cof}
	(i).\\
	(ii) Proof is the same as \ref{cof} (ii).
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and $I$ an ideal of $R$. Let $M$ be
	an $R$-module such that  $\dim M/IM \leq 1$ {\rm(}e.g.,
	$\dim R/I \leq 1${\rm)}. Then, the following conditions are equivalent:
	
	{\rm(i)} The $R$-modules $M$
	is an $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite.
	
	{\rm(ii)} The $R$-modules $H^i_I(M)$ are $I$-weakly cofinite for all $i$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) Follows by  Corollary \ref{cof2}.

(ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) It follows by \cite[Proposition 3.9]{Mel}.\qed

label: abel1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{abel1}
 Let $I$ be an ideal of a Noetherian ring $R$. Let   $\mathscr {FD}^1(R,I)_{ethwcof}$  denote the category of $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite and ${\rm FD_{\leq1}}$ ~ $R$-modules. Then
 $\mathscr {FD}^1(R,I)_{ethwcof}$
is an Abelian category.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $M,N\in \mathscr {FD}^1(R,I)_{ethwcof}$ and let $f:M\longrightarrow N$ be an
$R$-homomorphism. Since by \cite[Lemma 2.3 (v)]{AB} the class of ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$ is a Serre subcategory of the category of $R$-modules, it is enough  to show that the $R$-modules $\operatorname{Ker} f$ and
$\operatorname{Coker} f$ are $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite.

To this end, the exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow \operatorname{Ker} f \longrightarrow M \longrightarrow
\operatorname{Im} f \longrightarrow 0,$$ induces an  exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow {\rm Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{Ker} f) \longrightarrow {\rm
Hom}_R(R/I,M) \longrightarrow {\rm Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{Im} f )$$$$\longrightarrow
{\rm Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,\operatorname{Ker} f) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}^{1}_R(R/I,M),$$ that implies the
$R$-modules $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,\operatorname{Ker} f)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(R/I,\operatorname{Ker} f)$ are weakly Laskerian. Since $\operatorname{Ker} f$ is  ${\rm
	FD_{\leq1}}$~$R$-module, therefore it follows from Theorem \ref{wl} that $\operatorname{Ker} f$ is
 $I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite. Now, the assertion follows from the following exact
sequences
$$0\longrightarrow \operatorname{Ker} f \longrightarrow M \longrightarrow
\operatorname{Im} f  \longrightarrow 0,$$and
$$0\longrightarrow  \operatorname{Im} f \longrightarrow N \longrightarrow
\operatorname{Coker} f \longrightarrow 0.$$
head: environment

label: torext
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $N$ is finitely generated it follows that $N$ has a free resolution of
finitely generated free modules. Now the assertion follows using Theorem
\ref{abel1} and computing the modules ${\rm Tor}_i^R(N,M)$ and ${\rm
Ext}^i_R(N,M)$, by this
free resolution. \qed
head: manual

label: torextlc
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{torextlc} Let $\Phi$ be a system of ideals of  a Noetherian ring $R$, $M$ a non-zero
$I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite $R$-module such that $ \operatorname{H}^{i}_{\Phi}(M)$ are ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$~ $R$-modules for all $ i \geq 0$. Then for each finite
$R$-module $N$, the $R$-modules ${\rm Ext}^{j}_R(N,\operatorname{H}^{i}_{\Phi}(M))$ and ${\rm
Tor}^R_{j}(N,\operatorname{H}^{i}_{\Phi}(M))$ are $\Phi$-weakly cofinite and ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$~ $R$-modules for all $ i \geq 0$ and $ j \geq 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Apply Corollaries  \ref{torext} and \ref{cof}.\qed
head: manual

label: torextlc1
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{torextlc1} Let $\Phi$ be a system of ideals of  a Noetherian ring $R$, $M$ a non-zero
	$I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite $R$-module such that $\dim M/IM \leq 1$ {\rm(}e.g.,
	$\dim R/I \leq 1${\rm)} for all $I \in\Phi$. Then for each finite
	$R$-module $N$, the $R$-modules ${\rm Ext}^{j}_R(N,\operatorname{H}^{i}_{\Phi}(M))$ and ${\rm
		Tor}^R_{j}(N,\operatorname{H}^{i}_{\Phi}(M))$ are $\Phi$-weakly cofinite and ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$~ $R$-modules for all $ i \geq 0$ and $ j \geq 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By proof of Corollary \ref{cof2} (i) $\operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M))
\subseteq\underset{I \in \Phi}\bigcup \operatorname{Supp}_R(\operatorname{H}^{i}_I(M))$ and therefore
$$\operatorname{dimSupp} \operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M) \leq \sup \{ \operatorname{dimSupp} \operatorname{H}^{i}_{I}(M)| I \in
\Phi \} \leq 1,$$ thus $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ is ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$ $R$-module
and the assertion follows by  Corollary \ref{torextlc}.\qed
head: manual

label: torextlc2
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{torextlc2} Let $I$ be an ideal of  a Noetherian ring $R$, $M$ a non-zero
	$I$-$ETH$-weakly cofinite $R$-module such that $\dim M/IM \leq 1$ {\rm(}e.g.,
	$\dim R/I \leq 1${\rm)}. Then for each finite
	$R$-module $N$, the $R$-modules ${\rm Ext}^{j}_R(N,\operatorname{H}^{i}_{I}(M))$ and ${\rm
		Tor}^R_{j}(N,\operatorname{H}^{i}_{I}(M))$ are $I$-weakly cofinite and ${\rm FD_{\leq 1}}$~ $R$-modules for all $ i \geq 0$ and $ j \geq 0$.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
An $R$-module $M$ is called  $(I,J)$-weakly cofinite if
	$\operatorname{Supp}_R(M)\subseteq W(I,J)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/I,M)$ is a weakly Laskerian $R$-module, for
	all $i\geq0$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Let $I$ and $J$ be two ideals of $R$. Replacing $\Phi$ by $\tilde{W}(I,J)$, $\operatorname{H}^{i}_\Phi(M)$ by $\operatorname{H}^{i}_{I,J}(M)$ and $\Phi$-weakly cofinite module by $(I,J)$-weakly cofinite module, the Theorem \ref{homext} and  Corollaries \ref{cof}, \ref{cof2}, \ref{torextlc} and \ref{torextlc1} are true for local cohomology modules defined by a
	pair of ideals. Because by  \cite[{\it Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2}\rm]{TYY}, it is easy
	to see that the local cohomology modules defined by a pair of ideals is a special
	case of local cohomology modules with respect to a system of ideals.
head: environment
